name: Saanich

facts.text: Saanich protects arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew once they reach 2 m tall or 4 cm in diameter, which is far smaller than most neighbouring bylaws.
facts.excerpt: Arbutus, Garry Oak, Pacific Dogwood, and Pacific Yew ... at least 2m tall or 4cm in diameter
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: In Saanich, Douglas-fir, bigleaf maple and western redcedar are protected from 30 cm in diameter, and any other tree from 60 cm. Dead or dying protected trees still need a permit.
facts.excerpt: Any other tree with a diameter of 60cm or more
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: On Saanich lots inside a mapped Steep Slope Area, a permit may be needed for trees as small as 10 cm in diameter or 5 m tall.
facts.excerpt: 10 cm or more in diameter, or 5 metres in height, that are growing in a Steep Slope Area
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked); exact Saanich document for this line not confirmed

facts.text: Saanich is rewriting its tree bylaw. Until a new bylaw passes, the existing 2014 bylaw (No. 9272) still applies, and the June 2026 update says replacement planting will still be required.
facts.sourceTitle: Q&A: Tree Bylaw project update, June 2026 (District of Saanich)
facts.excerpt: the existing Tree Protection Bylaw will continue to apply until a revised bylaw passes
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Saanich's Streamside Development Permit Area covers land within 30 m of streams, ditches, ponds, wetlands and lakes. Work inside it may need a Streamside Development Permit, and Saanich suggests talking to Environmental Services (250-475-5471) first.
facts.sourceTitle: Streamside Development Permit Area | District of Saanich
facts.excerpt: applies to all streams, ditches, ponds, wetlands and lakes
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked); whether ordinary landscaping in the SDPA needs a permit was not confirmed

facts.text: Saanich's Pesticide Bylaw generally bans pesticides for lawns, trees, shrubs and flowers on residential land. A permit needs a certified applicator, and dandelions usually don't qualify.
facts.excerpt: usually the control of broadleaf weeds like dandelions do NOT meet the above conditions
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Owners must maintain the boulevard beside their Saanich property, and landscaping it needs a Boulevard Permit. Fences, rocks, retaining walls, hedges and parking pads are not accepted on a boulevard.
facts.sourceTitle: Boulevard Maintenance and Planting Tips | District of Saanich
facts.excerpt: Fences, individual rocks, parking areas, retaining walls and hedges on a boulevard do not qualify as acceptable landscaping features.
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Saanich is split by an Urban Containment Boundary. Outside it, around Prospect Lake and Blenkinsop for example, lots stay large and rural with rural servicing standards, so acreage and farm-edge properties are common.
facts.sourceTitle: Rural Saanich Local Area Plan (District of Saanich)
facts.excerpt: maintain large lot sizes, rural residential and agricultural land uses, and rural servicing standards outside the Urban Containment Boundary
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked); neighbourhood examples are our framing

facts.text: Invasive plants are a constant pressure in Saanich. The Pulling Together programme has more than 200 volunteers removing English ivy, Scotch broom and Himalayan blackberry in 44 parks and natural areas.
facts.sourceTitle: Volunteer for Pulling Together | District of Saanich
facts.excerpt: unites over 200 volunteers across 44 parks and natural areas
facts.note: from search snippet (official site could not be fetched from this session: host blocked)

facts.text: Regional (CRD, not municipal): from May 1 to September 30, lawns on the regional water supply may be watered two days a week by address (even: Wednesday and Saturday; odd: Thursday and Sunday). The day limits apply only to lawns.
facts.excerpt: The watering schedule days only apply to lawns!
